record.original_question: Does there exist a normalized Schauder basis of L1[0,1] that can be partitioned into two subsequences such that one subsequence is relatively weakly compact and the other is equivalent to the unit vector basis of ℓ1?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. [116] Does there exist a normalized basis of L1 which can be split into two subsequences, one of which forms a relatively weakly compact set and second is equivalent to the unit vector basis of `1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L^1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable functions on $[0,1]$ with norm $\|f\|_1=\int_0^1|f(t)|\,dt$. A sequence $(e_n)_{n\ge 1}$ in $L^1[0,1]$ is called a Schauder basis if every $f\in L^1[0,1]$ admits a unique representation $f=\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n e_n$ with convergence in norm; it is normalized if $\|e_n\|_1=1$ for all $n$. A subset $A\subset L^1[0,1]$ is relatively weakly compact if its weak closure is weakly compact (equivalently, $A$ is bounded and uniformly integrable). A sequence $(x_n)$ in a Banach space is said to be equivalent to the unit vector basis of $\ell^1$ if there exist constants $0<c\le C<\infty$ such that for every finitely supported scalar sequence $(a_n)$,
$$c\sum_n|a_n|\;\le\;\Big\|\sum_n a_n x_n\Big\|\;\le\;C\sum_n|a_n|.$$

Question: Does there exist a normalized Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of $L^1[0,1]$ together with a partition $\mathbb{N}=A\sqcup B$ into two infinite subsets such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the subsequence $\{e_n:n\in A\}$ is a relatively weakly compact subset of $L^1[0,1]$, and
\item the subsequence $(e_n)_{n\in B}$ is equivalent to the unit vector basis of $\ell^1$?
\end{enumerate}
